packageRules.description: Automerge patch updates for the media + keepers stacks (non-load-bearing apps). Uses matchFileNames with the REAL paths components/apps/{media,keepers}/** — the old matchPaths:[media/**,keepers/**] matched ZERO files (there is no root media/ or keepers/ dir), so this rule never fired and patch bumps were merged by hand. matchPaths is also deprecated.

Immich server + machine-learning MUST bump together (identical app version, or Immich breaks) and are reviewed, never automerged. repository: is set explicitly in components/apps/immich/values.yaml so the helm-values manager can resolve a datasource and track the app tag. A MAJOR bump (v3.x) is breaking (OAuth/API/env changes + forward-only DB migrations) and also wants a matching newer immich-charts chart -> do it by hand after a verified DB backup, not via a Renovate merge.

CNPG Postgres operand images: Renovate proposes MINOR updates only (since 2026-11-19), as one grouped PR, reviewed, never automerged. Tags are pinned to the Postgres minor (18.6, 18.6-1.1.1; floating 18 tags drifted per node, 2026-09-15). Docker versioning treats the vectorchord suffix (-1.1.1) as a compatibility string, so only the Postgres part moves; a vectorchord version change stays a manual job. The clusters use primaryUpdateMethod switchover, so a minor roll costs a switchover per cluster, not a ~4 min in-place restart.
prBodyNotes: After merge, on the immich-postgres primary as postgres superuser: `ALTER EXTENSION vector UPDATE;` if the new vectorchord build ships a newer pgvector (components/apps/immich/values.yaml). Check that all three clusters return to 2/2 healthy and ContinuousArchiving=True.

packageRules.description: A Postgres MAJOR (18 -> 19) is a database migration event, never a Renovate PR.

The barman-cloud plugin image (plugin-barman-cloud) is pinned to a vendored install manifest in components/operators/cnpg-barman-plugin/templates/plugin.yaml -> a tag bump alone would desync the manifest (same trap as sealed-secrets/rook), and the new plugin version must be re-checked against the running CNPG minor. Bumped by hand.

Rook is a manual, supervised, version-coherent bump (CLAUDE.md 'Upgrading Rook/Ceph'). Renovate must NOT auto-propose it: the 2026-06-12 v1.19.5->v1.20.0 auto-bump (#134) broke CSI (operator changed the CSI ServiceAccount naming, ceph-csi-*-sa went missing). Both charts bump together, by hand, after a helm-dependency-update chart-exists check + an oc-diff of the CSI SA/RBAC delta. ceph-csi-drivers (since Rook v1.20.9 the operator chart's CSI Driver subchart) is pinned to the ceph-csi-operator version that Rook release bundles (1.0.4 for v1.20.9) and moves with Rook; Renovate proposed 1.1.0 as #213 on 2026-11-05.

Ceph image bumps are gated on Rook<->Ceph compatibility (a Rook minor supports a bounded Ceph range; allowUnsupported:false refuses an unsupported Ceph) AND a planned degraded window (no drain headroom on the 3-OSD no-drain topology). Renovate must NOT auto-propose it; bump the Ceph image by hand only after the running Rook is confirmed to support the target. (Live example: #117 v19.2.4->v20.2.2 major Squid->Tentacle, unsupported by Rook 1.19.5.)

customManagers.description: node_exporter runs on the TrueNAS box as a CUSTOM (compose) app, so TrueNAS itself will never offer an update: custom apps have no catalog entry to compare against and app.query always reports upgrade_available=false. app.outdated_docker_images only helps for mutable tags like :latest, and this one is pinned. Renovate is therefore the ONLY thing that will ever tell us a newer image exists. The manager matches every `image:` line in the file rather than one named variable, so a future custom app is covered without editing it; catalog apps (garage, syncthing) have no image line and are tracked by TrueNAS instead. Applying the bump still needs an operator playbook run (--ask-vault-pass).
